docs.title: Glossary
docs.text:
Terms are Sanskrit unless marked (Ta. = Tamil, Ka. = Kannada, Pa. = Pali, Pk. = Prakrit, Ur. = Urdu/Persian, Hi. = Hindi, Ma. = Marathi, Mal. = Malayalam, Be. = Bengali, Gu. = Gujarati, Te. = Telugu).

Term Meaning abhaṅga (Ma.) Devotional song form of the Marathi Vārkarī poets abhidhā Denotation; the primary, conventional meaning of a word abhinaya Acting; of four kinds: bodily (āṅgika), verbal (vācika), costume and make-up (āhārya) and involuntary (sāttvika) akam (Ta.) “Interior”: classical Tamil poetry of love ākhyāyikā Prose narrative said to be told by the hero, based on real events (e.g. Bāṇa’s Harṣacarita) ākhyān (Gu.) Narrative poem retelling an episode of the epics or Purāṇas for public recitation (Premānand) alaṅkāra Ornament; a figure of speech alaṅkāraśāstra The science of poetics anubhāva Consequent; the outward sign of an emotion anuṣṭubh The eight-syllable quarter metre; the narrative śloka Apabhraṃśa The last stage of Middle Indo-Aryan, used in literature from c. 6th century arthaprakṛti The five elements of a dramatic plot (seed, drop, extended episode, brief episode, outcome) āryā A moraic metre, inherited from Prakrit gāthā poetry aucitya Propriety, fittingness avasthā The five stages of the hero’s action in a play bayāẓ (Ur.) A poet’s or reader’s personal notebook of verses bhakti Loving devotion to a deity bhāṇa One-act monologue play spoken by a man-about-town bhāva Emotional state camatkāra Aesthetic wonder or delight campū Narrative kāvya in mixed prose and verse citrakāvya “Picture poetry”; verse relying on verbal or visual patterning dāstān (Ur.) Long prose romance told in episodes by professional storytellers (dāstān-go) dhvani Suggestion; meaning conveyed beyond the expressed sense dīvān (Ur.) A poet’s collected lyric poems, arranged by the final letter of the rhyme dohā (Hi.) Rhymed couplet of North Indian poetry doṣa Fault of composition dṛśya kāvya “Poetry to be seen”: drama gadya Prose gāthā (Pk., Pa.) Verse; a stanza in the āryā metre ghazal (Ur.) Lyric of independent couplets sharing rhyme and refrain guṇa Quality or excellence of composition īhām (Ur.) Wordplay on a word with two meanings; the fashion of early Delhi Rekhta poetry inshāʾ (Ur.) The art of ornate letters and documents; model collections of letters jātaka (Pa.) Story of a previous life of the Buddha kathā Story; invented prose narrative (e.g. Bāṇa’s Kādambarī) kavi Poet kāvya Literature composed with conscious artistry khaṇḍakāvya Short poem (e.g. the Meghadūta) lakṣaṇā Indication; secondary meaning arising when the literal sense is blocked mahākāvya Court epic in cantos malfūẓ (Ur.) Recorded conversations of a Sufi master maʿnī-āfirīnī (Ur.) “Meaning-creation”: packing several layers of sense into a verse maṅgalkāvya (Be.) “Poem of blessing”: long narrative poem sung in honour of a deity such as Manasā or Caṇḍī maṇipravāḷam (Mal.) “Rubies and coral”: mixed Malayalam–Sanskrit literary idiom māppiḷappāṭṭu (Mal.) Song literature of the Māppiḷa Muslims of Kerala, in Arabi-Malayalam mārga “Way”: Daṇḍin’s two poetic manners, Vaidarbha and Gauḍa marsiya (Ur.) Elegy, above all on the martyrdom of Ḥusain at Karbala masnavī (Ur.) Long poem in rhyming couplets: romance, history or mystical teaching maẓmūn (Ur.) “Theme”: the conceit or proposition a verse develops muktaka Single self-contained stanza mushāʿira (Ur.) Assembly at which poets recite verses composed in a given metre and rhyme nāṭaka The principal type of play, on a legendary theme with a noble hero nāṭya Theatre; drama with music and dance nāyaka, nāyikā Hero, heroine nirguṇa, saguṇa Without and with attributes: devotion to a formless God and to God with form nīti Prudent conduct; policy; worldly wisdom padam (Te.) Short song for dance, often in the voice of a courtesan addressing the god as lover (Kṣetrayya) padya Verse phāgu (Gu.) Poem on the spring festival, often on an ascetic tempted by the season prabandha Composition; in Telugu, the long ornate narrative poem prakaraṇa Play with an invented plot and a hero of middle rank Prakrit (prākṛta) Middle Indo-Aryan literary languages pratibhā Poetic imagination, creative genius puṟam (Ta.) “Exterior”: classical Tamil poetry of war, kingship and public life qaṣīda (Ur.) Long monorhyme poem, usually of praise rasa Aesthetic experience of a generalised emotion; “flavour” rāsa (Gu.) Narrative or didactic poem for singing; the Jain rāsas are the earliest Gujarati literature Rekhta (Ur.) “Mixed”: eighteenth-century name of Urdu poetry and its language rekhtī (Ur.) Urdu poetry written by men in the idiom of women rīti Style; for Vāmana, the soul of poetry rūpaka Play (ten types); also metaphor sabk-i hindī (Ur.) “Indian style”: later name for the “fresh” Persian poetry of the 16th–18th centuries sādhāraṇīkaraṇa Generalisation; the freeing of an emotion from personal reference sahṛdaya The sensitive, responsive reader or spectator sandeśakāvya Messenger poem sandhi Juncture; the five structural divisions of a play sarga Canto of a mahākāvya ṣaṭpadi (Ka.) Six-line stanza, the principal narrative metre of medieval Kannada śataka A “century” of verses śleṣa Paronomasia; a word or phrase with two meanings śruti “What is heard”: revealed scripture, the Veda, which the theorists did not count as kāvya sthāyibhāva Stable or dominant emotion underlying a rasa stotra Hymn of praise to a deity, the Buddha or a tīrthaṅkara subhāṣita “Well said”: a gnomic or epigrammatic stanza sūkta A Vedic hymn sūtradhāra Stage manager and director who speaks the prologue takhalluṣ (Ur.) Pen-name, usually placed in the last couplet of a ghazal tāza-gūʾī (Ur.) “Speaking the fresh”: the poetics of novelty in Persian poetry tazkira (Ur.) Biographical dictionary of poets with selections of their verse tiṇai (Ta.) Landscape or situation associated with a phase of love or war uparūpaka Minor dramatic form vacana (Ka.) Rhythmic prose-poem of the Vīraśaiva devotees vākh (Kashmiri) Short verse of Lal Ded vakrokti Oblique or “crooked” expression vibhāva Determinant; the cause or occasion of an emotion vidūṣaka Brahmin jester of Sanskrit drama vyabhicāribhāva Transitory emotional state (thirty-three in Bharata’s list) vyañjanā The power of suggestion
